label: known
name: Platonic cosmic receptacle
mech: The dodecahedron, the Platonic solid tied to the cosmos, was made in Gaul and Britain as a material "receptacle" in Pythagorean-Platonic spirit, a philosophy Druids were said to admire. The twelve pentagonal faces embody the universe; holes and knobs are decorative or ritual variation, hence no standard sizes. A rod-shaped bone object beside the Gellep grave specimen suggests staff mounting, like a scepter of spiritual authority. Absence from Italy follows from its Celtic provincial origin.
value: It explains the geography, lack of wear, lack of standardisation and silence of texts. Proponents propose better-contexted finds and evidence of mounting.

label: known
name: Gallo-Roman divination and magic
mech: A private, non-official object of sorcery or fortune-telling, absent from literature and art because unofficial. Twelve faces echo zodiac or twelve-oracle systems like the Sortes Sangallenses and the zodiac-named Geneva die. In the Spindle-of-Necessity version, thread was wound across knobs and through holes to cast or read fate. Breakage and repair of finds such as Kortessem may mark ritual destruction.
value: It explains absence from texts, lack of wear and the Celtic-area distribution. Its test is thread or fibre traces on knobs and holes, and deposition patterns showing deliberate burial or breakage.

label: known
name: Farmer's sowing-date instrument
mech: Aimed at the sun and steadied on its knobs, opposite holes of different diameters act as apertures whose sunlight geometry marks the equinoxes and the autumn window for sowing winter wheat. Different hole pairs correspond to different dates or latitudes, which is why dimensions vary. It needed no markings, being a calendar-by-light.
value: It explains twelve differently sized holes, northern farming provinces and low wear (used a few days a year). Wagemans tested a bronze copy over several years at different latitudes.

label: known
name: Wax-forming tool
mech: Warm wax pressed into the hollow body through the holes forms discrete, repeatable wax elements, such as bullae securing cords or marking documents. Corner knobs act as spacers during compression and aid removal; aperture size controls thickness and the raised central boss. The tool turns a flexible craft action into a standard one.
value: It explains knobs, variable holes and the single wax-bearing specimen. Lamb's plastic trials produced repeatable forms; the proposed test is bronze replicas, wax-residue analysis and matching ancient sealings.

label: known
name: Coincidence rangefinder
mech: Looking through a face's small hole at a standard-sized object (a man, a standard, a pole) until it exactly fills the large opposite hole gives distance by proportion. The faces form pairs of differing diameters, giving a range of calibrated distances; knobs let it rest flat or be gripped. Finds at forts link it to military engineering or surveying, like the dioptra.
value: It explains the opposite-hole size contrast and finds in military camps. Sparavigna's test is measuring hole-pair ratios against plausible target sizes and ranges on real objects.

label: g1_crux
name: Axle-spun lot, size-coded holes
mech: A household oracle was threaded on an upright wooden or bone rod through the larger unringed opposite pair, which were its bearings. It was spun and read from whichever ringed hole stopped facing the consultant. The answer was that hole's size, so each object needs ten distinguishable diameters, never a scheme shared with others, and no letters. Rings frame the readable apertures; knobs give spinning grip and keep rims off surfaces. Soft rods and occasional private Gallo-British use leave bronze unworn and suit settlement finds and textual silence; the Gellep bone rod is its axle.
value: It alone makes within-object variation, no cross-object scheme, no inscriptions and the unringed pair all necessary. In Guggenberger's per-object measurements, if type-2a unringed pairs are often unequal or ringed holes on one object coincide within 0.5 mm, it is refuted.

label: g1_crux
name: Hand-tuned bronze vessel whistle
mech: Each piece was a Gallo-British edge-blown vessel flute: the player blew across one larger unringed hole, its opposite twin was a thumb vent, and the ring-marked holes were finger or wax stops. Pitch depends on open hole area against cavity volume, so graded holes give a fuller scale, and continuously varying bodies forced individual tuning, which rules out any shared hole standard. Knobs let it be held and set down without blocking holes. Wax, used to join and tune ancient pan-pipes, explains the German residue; lips and fingers leave bronze unworn; and the Kortessem repair restores airtightness.
value: It turns differing holes, continuous sizes, the unringed pair and the wax trace into requirements. Sound the intact Norton Disney piece with an artificial-mouth air jet across an unringed rim, other holes film-sealed: if no stable tone results, it is refuted.

label: g1_crux
name: Hole-signature membership token
mech: Each was a recognition token of a non-official Gallo-British association, its hole diameters a personal signature checked against a counterpart such as a pegged wooden gauge. A signature must vary within each object and never repeat between objects, exactly the observed pattern; the larger unringed opposite pair fixes the reference axis so the ten ringed sizes are read in order. Knobs and rings make imitation costly; shown rather than used, it stays unworn and uninscribed, while unofficial membership explains textual silence and spread from Gaul to Britain and beyond the frontier. Tokens followed owners into graves, hoards and rivers.
value: It makes the missing shared size scheme a design requirement and fits extra-imperial spread and valued deposition. Measure hole roundness on existing pieces: if scatter within single holes equals the steps between holes on one object, no signature exists and it is refuted.

label: g1_mech
name: Staff finial on tapering shaft
mech: A light insignia head was slid onto a staff through the larger unringed opposite pair and wedged where the taper met that pair's smaller hole, so opposite pairs may differ widely. Ringed holes faced outward as decorated windows; knobs were ornamental terminals shielding the head when grounded. Each head fitted its own staff, so no size scheme was needed. Carried occasionally, it stayed unworn, followed its holder into graves (the Gellep rod), hoards or rivers, and as an unofficial regional badge escaped texts and art.
value: It makes the unringed axis and unequal opposite pairs necessary, which symbolic and instrument readings leave unexplained. Under CT and microscopy, type-2a unringed pairs showing no more rim abrasion, organic traces or staining than ringed holes, or admitting no single tapering rod, refute it.

label: g1_mech
name: Touch-coded casting lot
mech: Tossed onto cloth, it tumbles on its knobs and settles with one face up. That face is read by its hole (size, ringed or not; the large unringed pair a distinct outcome), legible by eye or finger, so no letters were needed, and since each owner knew their own piece, neither a shared scheme nor fairness mattered. A light shell landing on cloth wears little. It belongs to north-western lot-casting (Tacitus describes Germanic lots thrown onto a white cloth), not Mediterranean dice culture, fitting distribution, civil and grave contexts and textual silence.
value: It explains why holes differ within each object yet share no scheme between objects, and why nothing is inscribed. On 10+ pieces, microscope knob tips against protected recesses: repeated tumbling polishes tips, so tips as fresh as recesses refute it.

label: g1_mech
name: Fumigation cage for aromatics
mech: Resin or herbs on a small ember went in through the largest hole; then it sat on a smaller-holed face, ember over that hole. Knobs lift it to admit air while upper holes vent smoke, and turning it to another face changes intake and smoulder rate, so holes needed only to differ within a piece; rings are ornament. The thin shell heats fast, knobs give cooler grips, use causes no wear, and the wax specimen is residue. Domestic, bath, theatre and funerary fumigation fits the mixed contexts, a regional form of a common rite, unnamed in texts.
value: It explains knobs as stand-offs, the perforated hollow and the wax specimen together, which symbolic and instrument readings do not. Clean interiors on 10+ pieces, with no soot, charred resin or heat tint and no resin markers by GC-MS, refute it.
